name: Scoliosis
definition: A three-dimensional spinal deformity characterized clinically by lateral curvature with vertebral rotation; causes and management differ substantially by age and etiology.

typical: Pain/function issues vary by age and etiology

redFlags.item: New neurological deficit, severe pain, constitutional symptoms or atypical curve features require evaluation for secondary causes

investigations.principle: Standing radiographs are used to characterize structural curves and measure magnitude when clinically indicated.
investigations.radiographs: Cobb-angle measurement and skeletal alignment guide classification/follow-up.
investigations.MRI: Not routine for every uncomplicated case; used when neurological or atypical features suggest intraspinal pathology.

green: Observation or scoliosis-specific rehabilitation according to age/curve/context
amber: Bracing/surgery thresholds depend on growth status, curve magnitude, progression, symptoms and etiology; specialist assessment is required for treatment decisions.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative pathways.

ayurvedaFramework.text: No single classical Ayurvedic disease is assigned as equivalent to scoliosis; deformity-related correlations remain unvalidated.

patientEducation.summary: A three-dimensional spinal deformity characterized clinically by lateral curvature with vertebral rotation; causes and management differ substantially by age and etiology.
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for new/progressive major weakness, gait deterioration, bladder/bowel dysfunction, saddle sensory loss, fever/systemic illness with severe spinal pain, or cancer-associated neurological symptoms.
